affected_condition: OpenSSL QUIC peer causes unbounded RETIRE_CONNECTION_ID queueing on retransmitted NEW_CONNECTION_ID frames
reason: Exact tools runtime inventory records no libmsquic paths. Tools execute fixed PostgreSQL TCP/local-socket clients, managed maintenance and filesystem operations, not an HTTP3/QUIC listener/client; no OpenSSL QUIC context or incoming stream policy is selected. No blanket absence-of-OpenSSL claim.
limitations: Exact supported image/source/configuration and current request/lifecycle callers only.
No package-wide fixed or absent-OpenSSL claim; unused native capabilities remain.
QUIC/DTLS integrations, custom native addons, direct PEM/SPKAC signing/base64 primitives, arbitrary caller lengths, plugins or operator crypto commands require reassessment.

affected_condition: Application calls EVP_EncodeBlock with a caller-provided length whose base64 output calculation exceeds signed int capacity
reason: No direct EVP_EncodeBlock call was found in retained Node crypto/ncrypto and reviewed .NET PAL source set. More importantly, supported app provides no raw native base64/PEM/SPKAC-signing API that forwards request-selected lengths to EVP_EncodeBlock. Normal HTTP/TLS certificate operations use bounded local trust/configuration inputs rather than caller-provided multi-gigabyte encoding lengths. Existing app artwork/body and credential/cookie paths do not expose this native encoding primitive. Internal OpenSSL PEM/base64 use is not declared absent; this is exclusion of the required oversized caller length.

affected_condition: DTLS endpoint reassembles attacker-controlled out-of-sequence handshake fragments with large declared lengths
reason: Supported web/maintenance network callers use TCP HTTP(S), SslStream and PostgreSQL local/TCP transport. Node TLS contexts and libpq source use ordinary TCP TLS methods; no DTLS constructor or datagram-secure transport is selected by application/entrypoints. UDP/dgram socket capability, if present in a runtime, does not by itself instantiate OpenSSL DTLS. This excludes the DTLS handshake reassembly caller, not ordinary TLS or all datagram capability.
